tasks.title: A timeline you can check
tasks.note: Principle: show the basis. A personal estimate by review stage, with how it was calculated one click away.
tasks.alt: The AI time tracker: 78 days of plan review, 13 days of corrections and 92 days in total, with the basis panel open and the review stages listed below.

pins.d: Built from this applicant’s own record and situation.
Similar permits, the current review queue, license status and how complete the application is.
Plan review, corrections and the total time to issue.
Each review stage with its dates. The current one is marked.

tasks.title: AI fills the form. The applicant decides.
tasks.note: Principle: AI fills, people decide. Upload the files once, fill the form in one click, then check and edit.
tasks.alt: The application form after AI autofill: a banner says 22 fields were filled, each filled field shows an AI icon, and the phone number has been edited by hand.

pins.d: Drawings, site plan and license already hold most answers.
AI reads the files and fills the form.
22 fields filled from the uploaded files.
The icon stays until the applicant changes it.
The applicant corrects anything AI got wrong.

tasks.title: A review that cites the code
tasks.note: Principle: cite the rule. Issues are flagged before submitting, each with the municipal code behind it.
tasks.alt: The AI review report: an expired-license flag on the application, and the flag panel open on the Seattle Municipal Code section it cites, with Accept and Dismiss buttons.

pins.d: Ranked as issue, warning or suggestion.
The flag sits on the exact field it’s about.
Each flag cites the municipal code and quotes the source.
Accept or dismiss. Flags are advisory.
Submitting waits until the critical issue is resolved.
